propositions: Line-start marker strings (VOTER_ERROR, MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR, RECONCILE_DEGRADED, ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR, LLM_TOKEN_USAGE) are emitted twice: once via logger and once via print(file=sys.stderr), causing journald to record duplicate entries with identical timestamps.

The observability probe in observability.sh anchors on line-start markers (e.g., grep -cE '^VOTER_ERROR {'), counting each real error twice because both logger and stderr outputs land in the combined journald stream.

Commit b0ac2544720 (ticket c130-6a87-531e-4441) activated configure_logging with a stdout StreamHandler, which wired the logger path for the duplicate marker emission; the dual emitter predates this change but only became problematic after logging configuration was enabled.

The fix keeps print(file=sys.stderr) as the sole line-start marker emission and changes logger calls to emit only the structured record body without the token prefix, ensuring exactly one countable line per real error.
Structural regression guards and new unit tests verify single emission for all five marker sites and prevent reintroduction of the dual-emission construct.
